Janakiballabh Roy Chowdhury, younger son of Ramakanta of Garuria. After his elder brother Ramballabh plotted to kill him, he fled to Murshidabad, where the Nawab made him zamindar of Arangpur pargana, and settled at Kalsakathi. The thirteen zamindar branches are his descendants. Last zamindar per Daily News Reel: Rajeswar Roy Chowdhury, who left for Kolkata after 1947.
A village of brick zamindar houses, compared with Panam Nagar; the main house is over 300 years old, brick and lime with terracotta work (district portal; Daily News Reel).
In ruins and unprotected: the main house is structurally standing but overgrown; one family still lives in part of it (Ajker Patrika 2022; district portal).

Department of Archaeology restoration began 4 May 2025; phase one (foundation, brickwork, Satkhira clay-tile roof, Tk 60 lakh) was reported complete in January 2026 (BSS). Chandradwip (Bakla) was a pre-Mughal principality; Kandarpanarayan moved its capital from Kachua to Madhabpasha around 1584 (Bangla Banglapedia). After Raja Ramchandra submitted to the Mughals in 1611 it became an ordinary zamindari. English Banglapedia says Madhabpasha became the head kachari of the former Raj from the early 19th century.

Dynasty: Danujamardana Deva by tradition (Banglapedia calls the story doubtful); Basu line from Paramananda Basu; Kandarpanarayan and Ramchandra. Zamindars after 1611 include Kirtinarayan, Premnarayan, Udaynarayan (Mitra), Shivnarayan, Lakshminarayan and Jaynarayan.
Surviving pieces per Bangla Wikipedia and Parjatan Bichitra (2025): a six-room building said to date from the 1800s and a two-storey Durga temple. Not described further.
Bangla Banglapedia says the Madhabpasha zamindar house and nearby Ramsagar Dighi are protected by the Department of Archaeology. Present condition not reported.
